messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] CRITICAL - Peregrine Financial (peregrine-eu3) p99 latency breach in eu-west-3 dedicated pool. p99 ~4.9s over 10m. Pager: ben_ops
ben_ops: picking up. starting triage. collecting p99/p95 graphs. @sara_sre oncall please join :phone:
sara_sre: here. I see tail spikes starting ~11:02 UTC. p95 steady at 1.2s, p99 4.5-5s. queue depth rising. tagging tom_rt for pool infra.
tom_rt: checking pool nodes for peregrine-eu3. CPU/GPU fine, but observed high retransmits between gateway -> runtime. NIC drops on node eu3-node-7.
ben_ops: any recent deploys or autoscale events?
claire_prod: customer indicates no changes. they reported slight error increase via support.
mike_platform: pulling router logs. there are bursts of grpc DeadlineExceeded from router to runtime around 11:03. also a couple of kernel panic traces on eu3-node-7 earlier.
olivia_support: looping in account team. @elaine-cs please prep customer note.
ben_ops: action plan: 1) cordon eu3-node-7, migrate its shards, 2) scale pool by +2 nodes temporarily, 3) apply per-tenant concurrency cap for Peregrine to reduce tail, 4) enable routing to warm-spare eu-west-2 if needed.
sara_sre: cordoning node now.
# command
```
rdwctl node cordon eu3-node-7 --pool peregrine-eu3 --reason "NIC flaps"
```
tom_rt: cordon sent. starting live shard migration.
ben_ops: migration in progress. monitoring backlog and p99.
tom_rt: migration finished, eu3-node-7 drained. we saw immediate drop in retransmits. p99 fell from 4.9s -> 3.4s.
mike_platform: scaling pool by +2 now.
# command
```
rdwctl scale --pool peregrine-eu3 --add-nodes 2 --type gpu-a10
```
claire_prod: asking customer to reduce concurrent batch size via SE to 6 while we stabilize.
olivia_support: customer accepted temporary cap and wants hourly updates.
ben_ops: concurrency cap applied server-side to Peregrine tenant:
```
rdwctl tenant update --tenant peregrine --pool peregrine-eu3 --concurrency 6
```
sara_sre: after scale and cap, p99 at 2.1s at 11:18 UTC. p95 1.0s. queue depth normal.
ben_ops: good. keep warm-spare routing in readiness but not flipped. add automated alert if p99 >3s for 10m.
mike_platform: created an alert rule:
```
rdwctl alerts create --name "peregrine-p99-failover" --expr "p99_latency > 3s" --for 10m --action runbook-failover
```
ben_ops: customer comm draft:
"We observed transient p99 latency due to a network interface instability on one of the dedicated nodes servicing your pool. We drained the affected node, added temporary capacity, and applied a short-term concurrency cap. Latency is back within SLA and we continue to monitor. We will provide a full RCA in 48h."
olivia_support: sent to customer at 11:23 UTC.
ben_ops: incident tagging: PEREG-2026-118. creating ticket with timeline and logs.
sara_sre: notes: eu3-node-7 NIC driver reported firmware error before panic. telemetry shows increasing packet drops leading to gRPC retries.
tom_rt: remediation: reprovision node with updated NIC firmware and kernel flags; run soak test before rejoining pool.
ben_ops: post-incident action items (owners):
- Reprovision eu3-node-7 with NIC firmware update (tom_rt, ETA 24h)
- Add automatic tenant migration when node-level retransmit rate > 0.5% (mike_platform, ETA 72h)
- Add per-tenant burst smoothing to prevent sudden batch storms (sara_sre, ETA 2 weeks)
- Customer RCA and scheduled follow-up call (olivia_support/claire_prod, ETA 48h)
- Add regression tests for node firmware compat (tom_rt, ETA 1 week)
All ack?
ben_ops: ack.
sara_sre: ack.
tom_rt: ack.
mike_platform: ack.
olivia_support: ack. scheduling RCA call for tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident PEREG-2026-118 status: mitigated -> monitoring. pagers cleared.
ben_ops: closing war room. keeping ticket open for postmortem and firmware work. thanks team :raised_hands:
claire_prod: customer confirms degradation resolved and thanked the team. end of thread.
